- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Introduction to the exhibition titled "Toys and Trinkets: A Subversion of Consumerism."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The exhibition aims to challenge dominant ideologies perpetuated by the toy industry and invites reflection on the relationship with play and consumption.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Each piece explores themes such as commodification of play, infantilization of adulthood, manipulation of cultural symbols, and environmental impact.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The first art piece, "MERDA Rug," is a handmade rug that appropriates the IKEA logo, replacing it with "MERDA," commenting on consumerism and societal impact.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The second piece, "Plastic Playtime," consists of toys made entirely of plastic, highlighting the contribution of plastic to waste and pollution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The third piece, "Greenwashing," is a mixed media work featuring posters from toy companies claiming to be environmentally friendly, exposing hypocrisy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The fourth piece, "Naive Nostalgia," includes paintings and drawings of childhood toys, reimagined to reveal the darker side of play.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The fifth piece, "The Infantilization of Adulthood," is a performance art piece featuring an adult performer playing with toys.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The sixth piece, "Ready-Made Rebellion," features altered toys and trinkets, challenging cultural symbols and commercialization.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The seventh piece, "Waste Not, Want Not," includes sculptures and collages made from discarded toy packaging, commenting on waste and pollution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The eighth piece, "Playful Protest," features photographs of individuals staging protests related to the toy industry and consumerism.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ninth piece, "The Dark Side of Play," is a film exploring exploitation, waste, and pollution in the toy industry.
